objective: Ship a golden-path dependency-cruiser config that enforces the layer rules of handbooks/architecture/clean-architecture-layers.md, run it in code-quality.yml only when a project has the config, test it in a dedicated Node CI job, and make the handbook state that CI enforces it.
why: ac5-1 to ac5-3 are not-verified. golden-paths/ holds only pipelines/, code-quality.yml has no dependency-cruiser step, and the handbook is advisory with no mention of CI. Rex reads diffs, not the import graph. The handbook bans SDK imports such as @aws-sdk in domain (line 39) and allows type-only imports across layers (line 43), so the rules must match both. o6 ac6-3 needs these rules.

include: golden-paths/typescript/.dependency-cruiser.cjs with rules for domain importing outside domain (including npm packages except an allowlist of pure libraries) and application importing infrastructure and circular dependencies
Exempt type-only imports from all three rules with dependencyTypesNot type-only
Resolve TypeScript path aliases through options.tsConfig
Match layer folders with (^|/)domain/ style paths and document how to adapt them
A step-level hashFiles condition in code-quality.yml that runs dependency-cruiser when the config is present and prints a notice when it skips and does not treat a skipped step as a failure
A shared skip-check script that both workflows and the test call
A fixture project with one violation per rule plus an aliased import and a type-only import and a clean case
A dedicated Ubuntu CI job with Node and a pinned tool lock that runs the fixture test
A line in clean-architecture-layers.md that keeps it advisory and states that CI enforces the layer rules when the config is present
exclude: Adding the config to existing managed projects
